base.description: The Lightspan MF-8 shelf kit as shipped: the fan module, the alarm module and two power modules fitted, and a dummy/filler board in each of the eight LT and two NT slots. This is the AA kit, with two 80 A power modules; the AB kit is the `kit-ab` configuration.
base.source: SOURCED: the shelf kit of UDS chapter 3, Table 4 (p24) - one LMFS-F, one LFAN-F, two LPWR-F and one LALM-F - with the dummy boards the installation manual requires in every unused slot. The kit ships without boards, so this base has no NT.

empty-shelf.description: The empty shelf LMFS-F, 3FE 79748 AA, as delivered: "without any module or board" (UDS s2.4), every slot open onto the backpanel.

front-cover.description: The shelf kit with the horizontal front dust filter assembly hung on the cover hook, as the installation manual's Figure 35 shows a horizontally mounted shelf with its cover closed. The cover is mandatory for EMC and comes in the horizontal mounting and front cover kits.

kit-ab.description: The Lightspan MF-8 shelf kit with the high-capacity feed, 3FE 79747 AB: the base kit with two 100 A power modules (LPWR-F AB, breaker marker "2X 50A") in place of the 80 A ones.

populated.description: The fully populated shelf of the data sheet's front render: eight LWLT-C multi-PON line boards and two LBNT-A NT boards, with the kit's fan, alarm and power modules.

datasheet.title: Nokia Lightspan Access Node MF-8 Unit Data Sheet Guide 26.9, 3HH-92646-AAAA-TQZZA Issue 09

description: The Nokia Lightspan MF-8 (LMFS-F), an 8RU fibre access node (OLT) shelf of the Lightspan MF family, drawn as it mounts horizontally in a 19-inch rack. Eight line-termination (LT) boards and two network-termination (NT) boards lie horizontally in the slot area, LT 8 at the top down to LT 1, then NT B, NT A, the alarm module and, at the bottom, two half-width power modules side by side. The fan module stands in an unlabelled slot at the left and exhausts the air drawn across the boards from the open right side. The front face is drawn with its two mounting flanges, because the left flange carries the dual-stud grounding point, the hook for the front cover and the ESD point. The shelf is cabled entirely from the front.

gaps.note: No rear view exists in the UDS, the USIM or the data sheet. UDS Figure 4 shows the six BATRET/FG fast-on pairs from the front, on the inner face of the backpanel; nothing shows the outside of the back.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the shelf's rear face

gaps.note: The left side's perforated field is placed by eye from perspective renders; the right side (the air intake) and the underside appear in no image held. UDS chapter 15 says the bottom dust filter assembly is fixed to "four screw holes in the bottom of the shelf" by four captive screws and three magnets, but their positions are not drawn.

gaps.note: UDS Figures 1 and 6 draw the right flange's four mounting slots open to the outer edge; the data sheet render draws them as closed oblong slots like the left flange's. Drawn closed.

gaps.note: The cover hook is absent from the data sheet render and is taken from UDS Figure 1 at about 2.2 px/mm; its shape is a bracket with a dark receptacle and two screws, no more than that.

gaps.note: No document held gives a power envelope for the whole shelf; USIM Table 21 gives figures per unit, and the LPWR-F rating is a current (80 A or 100 A), not a wattage.

alarm-slot.description: the alarm module slot (ALM) under NT A, 24.5 mm pitch

covers.description: the front cover of the horizontal mounting and front cover kits

esd.description: the ESD point on the left flange (UDS Figure 3)

fans.description: the single, unlabelled fan module slot at the left; six blowers in one module

grounding.description: the dual-stud chassis grounding point on the left flange, and its earth symbol

lt-slots.description: the eight LT (line termination) slots, 24.5 mm pitch, LT 1 at the bottom of the block to LT 8 at the top (UDS Figure 3). LT 1 and LT 2 are the hybrid NTIO / LT slots; no NTIO board exists in this release (UDS s2.4.1 Note 4)

nt-slots.description: NT A (rel-pos 1) and NT B (rel-pos 2), the two network-termination slots, 35 mm pitch

attrs.redundancy-note: UDS s2.4.1: two (redundant) power modules, "The two power modules provide power redundancy to the shelf"; s2.6: the shelf is fed from the active one

power-slots.description: the two half-width power module slots along the bottom, PWR 1 at the left

name: lmfs-f

airflow.note: USIM s4.1.3.4 (p153): the forced air "comes in via the open side and goes out via the fan", which is right to left in a horizontal mounting and bottom to top in a vertical one; s2.3.8.1 says the same, "Air intake at the right and air exhaust at the left (via the fan)". The top-cover legend "<- AIRFLOW" points the same way. UDS s11.3 (p80) gives only the vertical case. Air baffles can turn the flow front-to-rear or front-to-top (USIM s2.3.6, s2.3.8); the bare shelf is side to side.

bottom-dust-filter.note: The bottom dust filter assembly (3FE 79983 AA, UDS chapter 15: 358 W x 89 H x 284.85 D) is "a mandatory element when installing a Lightspan MF-8 vertically" and "can only be used in case of a vertical mounting configuration" (s15.3, s15.6). In that mounting it sits under the shelf's right-hand end, the air intake, across the 355 dimension; it is not part of a horizontally mounted shelf and is not drawn on any face here. The DS's "Height (w/o bottom dust filter assembly): 355 mm" is the same statement.

chassis.note: UDS s2.5.1 (p19), repeated for the kits in s3.5.1 and s4.5.1: height 355 mm (8 RU), width "overall over flanges: 481 mm" and "no flanges: 448 mm", depth "front plate to rear: 246 mm" and "including grounding stud: 262 mm"; with a power module 274 mm and with the front dust filter assembly 290 mm. s2.5.2: 11.5 kg empty; s3.5.2: 16.75 kg as a kit. The DS prints a mounting centre distance of 465 mm and an overall depth of 287.3 mm, which matches none of the UDS depths and is carried as the DS's own figure. The chassis width is the 448 body; the front view alone is 481 wide, see flanges.

colour.note: DS render, averaged over plain areas: flange 95,102,111 (#5f666f), fan cover and frame 86,95,106 (#565f6a), right legend strip 67,74,82. A vendor render, so this is the vendor's presentation of a blue-grey slate finish; no photograph of a unit is held.

columns.note: Across, on the DS render: flanges 0-16.5 and 464.5-481.0; the fan cover between shadow lines at 17.7 and 55.2, in which the stated 38.1 x 348.5 fan module (UDS s11.6.1) is centred at x 17.4, y 3.2; a legend strip 55.7-58.5; board faceplates from 59.0 to 459.5 (400.5, the boards being 388 long with their ejector ends); a second legend strip 460.0-462.2. Power bay frame verticals at 63.2, 259.25 and 455.6, so the two bays are at x 63.1 and 259.25.

defaults.note: The base is the shelf kit as UDS chapter 3 and Table 4 (p24) deliver it - the fan module, the alarm module and two power modules fitted, "without boards" - with a dummy board in every LT and NT slot, because USIM s4.4 forbids operating the shelf with an empty slot. It has no NT board and so cannot be logged into; it is the orderable starting point and not a working node. The populated example is the DS render's population.

flange-holes.note: DS render, hole centres: left flange a round hole 6.1 across at (8.0, 14.6) and at (8.0, 340.1), and four oblong slots 9.4 x 6.1 at y 37.8, 139.3, 215.7 and 317.4; right flange the same four slots at x 473.0. The centres are 465 apart, the DS's mounting centre distance. UDS Figures 1 and 6 draw the right flange's four slots open to the outer edge, as notches; the DS render draws them closed. Drawn closed, as measured; see the gap.

flanges.note: The front view is drawn 481.0 wide WITH the two mounting flanges, 16.5 mm each ((481 - 448) / 2; the DS render measures 16.5), against the library's rule that ears are not drawn. The reason is that this shelf's left flange is not bare: UDS s2.4 (p16) lists on it, from bottom to top, a dual-stud chassis grounding point, a hook for the cover of the front dust filter assembly and an ESD protection point. Those parts are placements here and they need the flange to stand on. The rear, top and bottom views are the 448 body.

front-cover.note: Two front covers exist and they are different parts. The VERTICAL front dust filter assembly (3TJ 00003 AA, UDS chapter 16: 355 W x 542 H x 42.13 D) fits only a vertically mounted shelf, where it also spans the bottom dust filter assembly. The HORIZONTAL front dust filter assembly (USIM s2.3.7.1, p72-74: 355 H x 507.6 W x 36 D) is the one for the horizontal mounting drawn here and is nokia/mf8-horizontal-front-cover@1, placed only in the front-cover configuration. USIM s2.3.7.1 puts its right edge 55 mm beyond the right mounting holes, so on this face it runs from x 20.4 to 528: it overhangs the right flange by 47 mm, onto the cable tray of the same kit, which is not part of the shelf and is not drawn. Its small light window lands on the fan module's location lamp, which checks the position.

ground-pair.note: THE TWO-POINT CHASSIS GROUNDING POINT IS ONE PAIR (#828, #830): common/ground-stud-pair-5-8-m6@1, two M6 pan heads 12.0 across (the render's capped rounds measure 12.1), at rotate 90 and centred on the rendered studs' midpoint, (7.7, 247.55). Formerly two common/ground-stud@1 placements 16.3 apart. THE PITCH IS DRAWN 15.875, THE 5/8 IN. OF THE stud-pair-5-8 INTERFACE, NOT THE 16 THE MANUAL PRINTS: USIM s4.5.2.2 gives the lug's hole spacing as "16 mm (0.63 in.)" beside a stud hole of "6.35 mm (1/4 in.)", an inch-series lug whose 0.63 in. is 5/8 in. (0.625) rounded to two places, the figure lug makers print for that spacing; 16 mm is that rounding converted. A two-hole lug seated on the pair leaves its wire down the flange. The ESD point moved out of `grounding` into a group of its own, `esd` (#866).

ground-stud-size.note: USIM s4.5.2.2 recommends a dual-hole M6 lug cable with a stud hole of 6.35 mm (1/4 in.) and a hole spacing of 16 mm, on 3 AWG cable, for the two-point chassis grounding point, and says a single-lug cable will also work: the `stud-size` of ground-studs, the pair.

left-flange.note: DS render, centres from the shelf's top-left: a ringed round label 12 across at (7.9, 92.9), read as the earth bonding point label of USIM Figure 81; the ESD point, a white round 14.3 across, at (7.7, 115.3) (UDS Figure 3 points "ESD point" at this one); the two grounding studs, 12.1 across in their caps, at (7.7, 239.4) and (7.7, 255.7), 16.3 apart; the earth symbol, 8.3 across, at (7.9, 285.6). The library's common parts are placed on those centres and are smaller than the capped rounds the render draws (jack 6.0, symbol 6.0); the studs are one pair now, on their midpoint at the 5/8 in. pitch (ground-pair). The cover hook is NOT in the DS render; it is taken from UDS Figure 1 (p14), scaled by the flange slots it shares with the render (2.232 px/mm): a bracket about x 2.5-13.5, y 149-208, with a dark receptacle at y 162.4-196.0 and a screw at each end, at y 154.2 and 202.5. Good to about a millimetre.

nt-redundancy.note: UDS s2.4.1 Note 1: "The two NT boards provide NT redundancy to the shelf"; minimum one NT, maximum two. USIM s2.2.1.3 A: active/active on the data plane and active/standby on the control and management plane.

occupants.note: USIM Table 5: LT boards LGLT-D, LWLT-C, LLLT-A and LLLT-B, NT board LBNT-A (AA and AB), fan LFAN-F, power LPWR-F (AA 80 A, AB 100 A), alarm LALM-F, and the dummy boards LMDB-B EA (LT) and LMDB-E BA (NT); note 6, "no dummy panels exist for any of the modules". Only LWLT-C is modelled of the LT boards. UDS s2.4.1 Note 4: "In this release no NTIO boards are supported yet", so the two hybrid slots accept LT boards only. The slots are keyed: an NT dummy does not fit an LT slot (USIM Procedure 35 Note 2).

overhang.note: USIM s2.3.7.1 (p72-74) puts the horizontal front dust filter assembly's right edge 55 mm beyond the right mounting holes, which on the 481 mm face drawn here is 47 mm past its right end (front-cover). Nothing reaches past the left. The cover is placed only in the front-cover configuration, and the reach is stated so that its drawing past the flange is a claim and not a stray `at` (#865).

panel-scale.note: Gate 1. The DS front render is 1053 x 777 px. The shelf's outer flange edges are 872 px apart, which against the stated 481.0 is 1.8129 px/mm; at that scale the shelf measures 355.2 tall against the stated 355, and the two power modules 43.5 tall against the stated 42.8, so the render is orthographic and carries geometry at about 0.55 mm a pixel. It is a vendor render and not a photograph. UDS Figure 5 (p19) is a line drawing of the same face at 1.02 px/mm, used only to confirm the arrangement.

power.note: DS: "DC-powered: 48/60 V DC nominal; Fully redundant power feeding (branch A and B)". UDS s2.6 (p19): everything in the shelf is fed over the backpanel "from the active power module"; s2.4.1 Note: "The two power modules provide power redundancy to the shelf". USIM s2.2.1.3 C: "When two power modules are equipped ... power redundancy is supported". USIM s3.2.5.4 limits the feed to 80 A with two LPWR-F AA and 100 A with two LPWR-F AB. No document held states a power figure for the whole shelf: searched the DS, UDS chapters 2 to 4 and the USIM for "power consumption", "dissipation" and "W"; USIM Table 21 (p123) gives a figure per unit only, and each is carried on that unit's own contract.

rear.note: No document held draws the rear of the shelf. UDS s2.4.3 (p18) puts the "six BATRET (battery return) / FG (Frame Ground) fast-on combinations in the bottom right side of its backpanel", but Figure 4 shows them from the FRONT, through the empty slot area, on the inner face of the backpanel behind the alarm row: they are reached with the boards out and are not a rear-panel feature. The rear view is therefore sized from the top view and left empty.

rows.note: Row boundaries read on the DS render as the bright lower edge of each board's faceplate, at y 27.6, 52.4, 76.7, 101.2, 125.8, 150.3, 174.9, 199.7, 234.7, 269.7 and 292.9, then set to the vendor's stated pitches: LT and alarm 24.5 mm, NT 35 mm (UDS board chapters; USIM s4.4.6 for the dummy boards). LT 8 starts at 3.0 under the top rail, the LT block ends at 199.0, NT B 199.0-234.0, NT A 234.0-269.0... the alarm row is seated at 269.5-294.0, half a millimetre lower than the stack gives, where the render has it. A dark rail 4.4 mm tall separates the alarm row from the power bays, whose white frame ticks are at y 297.9 and 341.7: the bays are the stated 196.15 x 42.8 (UDS chapter 13) at y 298.4. Below them the shelf's bottom rail runs to 355.

sides.note: No document held draws either side face. Vendor renders of a vertically mounted shelf show its upper face - the shelf's LEFT side, behind the fan module - perforated over most of its area, which is the fan exhaust; the field is placed by eye from those perspective views. The right side is "the open side" the air enters by (USIM s4.1.3.4) and no image held shows it.

slot-legends.note: The legends are printed in the two narrow strips left and right of the boards, reading bottom to top, about 2.2 mm high: LT 8 to LT 3, NT B, NT A, ALM, and PWR 1 (left strip only) and PWR 2 (right strip only). Positions measured on the DS render: each LT and ALM legend about 3.9 below its row's top, each NT legend 9.4 below, the PWR legends at mid-height. For the two hybrid rows UDS Figure 1 (p14) prints the longer "NTIO 2 / LT 2" and "NTIO 1 / LT 1", as s2.4.1 says the slots are labelled, while the DS render prints "LT 2" and "LT 1". The UDS wording is used, as the unit's own document; see the gap. Legends smaller than this on the render (none found on the frame) would not resolve at 0.55 mm a pixel.

slot-order.note: UDS Figure 3 "Board and module positions in LMFS-F" (p16) and USIM Figure 6: from the top LT 8 to LT 3, NTIO 2 / LT 2, NTIO 1 / LT 1, NT B, NT A, ALM, then PWR 1 at the left and PWR 2 at the right, with the fan area at the left. UDS s2.4.1 (p16-17) says the same in words, from the bottom up.

sources.note: Written first, before any number. UDS = Lightspan Access Node MF-8 Unit Data Sheet Guide 26.9, 3HH-92646-AAAA-TQZZA Issue 09: chapters 2 to 4 (p13-32) the shelf and its two kits, Figures 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6; chapter 11 the fan module; chapters 15 and 16 the bottom and the vertical front dust filter assemblies. USIM = Lightspan Access Node MF-8 User, Safety and Installation Manual 26.9, 3HH-92647-AAAA-RJZZA Issue 09: s2.2 and s2.3 (Table 5, the orderable items), s2.3.7 the horizontal mounting and front cover kits, s2.4.5 Table 21 power per unit, s4.1.3.4 airflow, s4.4.6 the dummy boards. DS = Nokia Lightspan MF-8 data sheet CID214273 (April 2025), with a front render of a fully populated shelf. Every figure in the two guides is an embedded raster of 1 to 3 px/mm, and every image of the shelf is a vendor render: no photograph of a unit is held.

top.note: UDS Figure 5 (p19; the same art is Figures 10 and 15), the plan drawn above the front view, an embedded raster at 1.019 px/mm, so positions are good to about a millimetre. It is drawn with the FRONT edge uppermost and the shelf's left at the left (the grounding stud projects from the upper left corner, in line with the left flange of the front view below it), and its AIRFLOW legend is upside down in the figure. USIM Figure 83 (p153) shows that legend on the shelf's top cover, near the front edge behind the fan partition, reading "<- AIRFLOW" from the front. The 38 screw heads and the legend are transcribed with the rear at y 0. A small rectangle the drawing has near the front left corner (x 14-27, 3-10 mm from the front) is not identified and is not drawn.
